study.question: Authorized validation only. baseline-din macro AUC 0.8099233880793816 / macro Logloss 0.05662295138414975. g3-r0000-task_action_relevance 0.8114567735949517 beat shared action 0.8111539425334561 and both item-only controls (0.8071249582677915 / 0.8068573952810285). g3-r0001-feedback_context/support and reversed controls all underperformed their parent (macro 0.8102586596759266 to 0.8105780168237375): extra grouping did not establish beneficial task semantics. g3-r0002-peer_detached/joint and self_detached/joint (0.8112515517652337 to 0.8114146033770447) all remained below that parent: peer exchange did not establish a gain. g3-r0003-private_relevance 0.8120988583659786 beat partial 0.8117084621515915 and uniform 0.8113736080464058, with identical capacity among those cells; incumbent replay exactly reproduced 0.8114567735949517. g3-r0004-all_score_live exactly reproduced private_relevance. g3-r0004-click_score_stop reached 0.8123335254548857 / 0.05665085308601132; versus all_score_live AUC deltas [click,cart,fav,buy] were [+0.0009945396558854,+0.0000940022605153,-0.0001462207694214,-0.0000036527913509]. aux_score_stop and all_score_stop reached only 0.8112808667206706 and 0.8117661643506242; purchase AUC fell to 0.864841196901355 and 0.8663710068363274 versus live 0.8707734952073054. Click stop is a small single-seed gain, with a favorite trade-off, not repeated evidence of negative transfer. Relative to baseline-din, click_stop task AUC deltas were [+0.0022157150775016,+0.0034483667606067,+0.0033889003035821,+0.0005875673603262], Logloss deltas [-0.0002849766035991,+0.0000642026191121,+0.0000309404055809,+0.0003014403863523]. Its AUC is higher but macro Logloss remains 0.0000279017018616 above baseline. Empty-history macro AUC 0.7185076099922739 is below baseline 0.7268428930232654; small positive counts (45 cart,28 fav,13 buy) limit interpretation. Latest knowledge usage declared DIN inheritance and considered forward interaction architectures; executed g3-r0004 sources changed backward connectivity only. No hub or peer-transfer mechanism was established by that declaration. No failed receipts or previous runtime error are supplied; all 21 indexed trials succeeded. Failed implementation is not inferred from a null metric. Raw parquet and torch are unavailable in this coding environment: inherited host protocol/data identity and committed receipts establish the available starting point; new runtime validity remains pending. Question: Is the click-score input-stop gain localized to gradients through target queries, through historical keys/actions, or their interaction, while auxiliary relevance learning stays intact?
study.hypothesis: Working query-dominant hypothesis: click target-conditioned relevance gradients can disrupt the shared target embedding geometry, while history-side relevance gradients may remain useful. Stopping only query-role click gradients could retain the click improvement without the favorite trade-off. This is provisional: gradient conflict was not measured; history-dominant, joint-interaction and no-reproducible-effect alternatives remain admissible. Shared tables mean role-specific interventions affect all tasks indirectly.

study.proposed_difference: Two boolean switches detach click query operands or historical key/action operands BEFORE forming [q,k,q-k,q*k,a]. Keep live values and direct target/context paths, and leave all auxiliary relevance gradients attached. All four standalone cells construct one common live interaction tensor and one equal-valued click-role tensor with identical arithmetic and no added parameters. Full detachment after forming interactions is decomposed into roles without changing forward information. Both/neither endpoints should reproduce existing click-stop/all-live trajectories subject to host numerical checks. Before any host training, verify four finite [B,1] probabilities and sum-BCE backward; labels never enter forward; target-action independence; masked item/action ID invariance in train/eval with cloned RNG/state; empty/full/holey masks and length-zero handling; label-order independence by consistent tower/trunk/output-row remapping. Verify exact parameter names/shapes/count (expected 32144072 total, 31793216 embedding, 350856 dense), separate private-trunk buffers, identical parameter tensors/RNG after construction in all four cells. At identical states, compare all cells forward and Dice-buffer updates in FP32 atol1e-6/rtol1e-5, BF16 atol2e-3/rtol1e-2. Compare both_stop with history_g3_r0004_click_score_stop.py and neither_stop with history_g3_r0004_all_score_live.py under matching configs in train/eval; require forward/state/gradient parity within those tolerances. For click score-only gradient probes use synthetic independent leaf target, keys, actions, and a score sum BEFORE bmm; test Q-block => no query leaf gradient, H-block => no key/action leaf gradient, live role => finite nonzero gradient on nondegenerate fixture; all relevance weights remain trainable, auxiliary score inputs remain live. Test all four cells, not aggregate embedding gradients: shared tables receive other paths. Use a separate pooled-value/readout probe to confirm both_stop still sends click gradients into values and direct target/context; stopping an entire embedding table is a bug. Check inherited masked query contribution to Dice statistics is held fixed, not repaired here. Checks have not run locally because torch/framework are absent. A host parity or gradient failure blocks efficacy attribution; retain its cost and do not train a failing cell.
predictions: Predeclared directional prediction: query_stop improves macro AUC over neither_stop; query-stop effects are positive conditional on both H settings, with the mean Q effect larger than mean H effect. These are directional mechanism predictions, not a minimum gain/veto for selection.
Query_stop matches or exceeds the incumbent both_stop macro AUC while its favorite AUC is closer to neither_stop; failure of this trade-off prediction weakens the query-only explanation.

At initialization all four cells have equal predictions, train/eval buffers and parameter counts. Both_stop and neither_stop should reproduce their corresponding historical endpoint scores; measured costs among the new cells will differ only through backward graph work and noise.

With Mqh denoting each metric for Q=q,H=h, report query main effect ((M10-M00)+(M11-M01))/2, history main effect ((M01-M00)+(M11-M10))/2, and interaction M11-M10-M01+M00 for macro and all four task AUC/Logloss. No significance claim from this one-seed factorial.
falsifiers: Any runtime parity failure, unexpected new parameter/RNG change, leakage, or wrong gradient path invalidates causal interpretation; stop that cell and preserve charged failure receipt.

If query_stop fails to beat neither_stop and has no positive conditional query effect, the query-dominant hypothesis is unsupported. If history_stop carries the improvement and Q does not, favor history-role explanation.
If only both_stop helps and partial cells do not, single-role sufficiency is falsified locally; a Q-by-H interaction remains possible.
If endpoints fail to reproduce within host observed tolerances despite passing forward/gradient checks, treat findings as execution/numerical instability, not mechanism proof.
If a later paired validation repetition reverses the effect, downgrade controlled support to unstable evidence. No withheld outcomes may inform that follow-up.
alternative_explanations: One seed with adaptive validation reuse; repeat paired seeds before generalization or significance claims.
Target and history share embedding tables. Role paths do not identify disjoint parameter groups or prove cross-task gradient conflict.
H bundles item-key and historical-action paths. A history effect cannot yet be attributed to one of these.
Stopping gradients changes optimization and implicit regularization, and BF16 sparse-gradient accumulation can cause small numerical differences.
Dice statistics include masked query positions, an inherited behavior held fixed; empty-history changes can arise through shared parameter training.
This tests a gradient mechanism within DIN adaptation, not superiority over full unified Transformer architectures.
Forward task conditioning/action inputs already explain much of the improvement over the initial DIN reference; this study only addresses the smaller within-private-scorer stop-gradient effect.

Reduced click-induced gradient magnitude acts as ordinary regularization rather than resolving antagonistic cross-task directions. A future authorized gradient diagnostic or matched scaling control would be needed to distinguish these.
